courses.description: This course deals with the rules of commercial companies in the United Arab Emirates under the Federal Commercial Companies Law with a focus on the most prominent legal issues and their impact on the applied practical reality to focus on the weaknesses and strengths of the UAE legislation and the ability of the company law rules to keep pace with the challenges and prospects of modern economic life. This course also aims to develop the students' ability to think objectively and analytically by encouraging them to criticize and judge the legal text. As such, this course also examines the latest amendments to the Companies Law to study and analyze them. The course then details the legal principles and rules governing each type of company, whether in terms of establishment or management, in addition to the rules of merger, acquisition, and liquidation for all companies, in addition to bankruptcy law as it applies to companies.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT227 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT227 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Commercial Arbitration Law
courses.description: This course introduces the legal framework for Arbitration, its main types, nature and characteristics. Topics include: the composition of the arbitral tribunal; forms and substance of an arbitration agreement; qualifications, jurisdictions and responsibilities of arbitrators; the arbitral procedures, the challenge, recognition and enforcement of arbitral awards.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT227 with a minimum grade D; PRVT302 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT227 with a minimum grade D
PRVT302 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: The Law of Execution
courses.description: This course introduces the students to the Law of Compulsory Execution of Judgement. It covers all legal aspects that follow the rendition of the judgement. This includes the study of the compulsory execution of the judgment based on its core pillars, i.e. the Writ of Execution and the Judge of Execution. In addition, it covers the subject of Summary Execution, along the methods of execution, its procedures and disputes; until ending with the Allocation of the Execution Proceeds.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT302 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT302 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Private International Law
courses.description: The Private international law course involves the study of the applicable law in private international relations; civil, commercial and personal status relations; the conditions of court jurisdictions in disputes involving foreign subjects and the applicable procedural law in this respect and the execution of foreign judgments.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT302 with a minimum grade D; PRVT307 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT302 with a minimum grade D
PRVT307 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Maritime and Aviation Law
courses.description: This course discusses the following topics: aircraft registration, the legal status of aircraft and the crew, leasing, purchasing, mortgaging, and insuring of the aircraft. Carriage by air. This course also examines the relevant international agreements that regulate civil aviation. The course also addresses the liability arising from damages caused by autonomous ships or aircraft and examines the European liability rules concerning artificial intelligence related to maritime and air transport.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT338 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT338 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Nominated Contract (Sale, Lease & Construction)
courses.description: The course is designed to study the contracts of sale, lease and construction in terms of their formation, effects (obligations of both parties), and termination. It deals also with the different relationships in the construction industry and the nature of electronic sale contracts and real estate contracts on maps. Finally, this course analyses the relevant rules of UAE law relating to such contracts.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT307 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT307 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Commercial Papers & Banking
courses.description: It includes a study of: commercial papers: the bill of exchange, the promissory note, and the check. Legal and Sharia aspects of banking business: bank deposits, bank transfers, current accounts, bank credits, operations on commercial papers, including electronic operations.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT338 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT338 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Rights in Rem
courses.description: This course deals with original real rights based on a definition of real rights and their characteristics, and a definition of the right of ownership, its elements, scope, and the legal restrictions pertaining to it. Furthermore, this course explores the jointly held property and its division, family property and its rules, and the common ownership and its rules. It also shed light on the different causes of acquiring property, and the reasons for the termination of ownership. Finally, the course addresses the rules of credit guarantees and the legal regulation relating to mortgages and the rights to privilege.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT307 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT307 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Intellectual Property Laws
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with the fundamental aspects of Intellectual property rights under UAE law and international agreements. It covers topics of copyrights, trademarks, geographical indications, Patents, industrial designs, lay-out design of integrated circuits, and the protection of plant varieties. The course focuses on both national and international legal rules governing intellectual property.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT227 with a minimum grade D; PRVT338 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT227 with a minimum grade D
PRVT338 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Civil Law
courses.description: This course addresses the recent trends in civil liability according to Emirati law while shedding light on the provisions of comparative law. The course delves into the study of civil liability provisions with a focus on its effects, particularly compensation in terms of its types and how it is estimated, in addition to studying the subject from a comparative perspective. Then, the course explores the modern applications of civil liability through studying civil liability for medical errors committed by robots, civil liability for accidents caused by self-driving cars, civil liability for copyright infringement when using artificial intelligence applications like ChatGPT, civil liability for environmental damages, civil liability for climate change, and civil liability for breaches of personal data.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Commercial Law
courses.description: This course includes studying the legal organization of one of the topics of commercial law in an in-depth manner, such as the company contract, for example, by studying the provisions and details of each company contract separately, with a focus on the most significant legal issues and their impact on the practical and applied reality, with the aim of shedding light on the weaknesses and strengths of the UAE legislation and determining the extent to which the rules of company law keep pace with the challenges and prospects of modern economic life. This course also aims to develop the student's ability to think objectively and analytically by developing his scientific research skills and encouraging him to criticize and judge the legal text. In this sense, this course also examines the difficulties facing the idea of the one-person company and its applications in comparative law and its impact on the general security of the company's creditors. This course also addresses the latest amendments to the Companies Law, especially regarding direct foreign investment, in order to critically examine the adequacy of incentives in this regard.

courses.title: International Trade Contracts (E)
courses.description: This course familiarizes the students with rules that are applicable in international trade contracts. In this context course provides information related to the UN CISG Rules, UNIDROIT Principles, difference between CIF and FOB Contracts, Hardship and Forcemajeure Clause, damages under UNCISG, Bill of Lading and Letters of Credits. The knowledge of this course enables the students to negotiate and draft international trade contracts, prepare pro forma invoice, understanding of Bill of Lading, and what are the different modes of contracts governing Transport of Goods when the trading is international level (Transport by Air, rail, road and sea).

courses.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution (E)
courses.description: The object of the course is to study methods of resolving disputes other than by litigation in courts. The course will include the main aspects of arbitration agreement, the differences between arbitration and conciliation, the differences between national and international arbitration, arbitration procedures, applicable law, and arbitration award enforcement.

courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: The student is committed to conduct original research on a vital topic of private law under the supervision of his or her academic supervisor, which will be presented in the form of a thesis written according to a publishable standard. The writing stage must be preceded by holding a seminar for the student to discuss the topic of the thesis with the relevant faculty members in a public session. During the writing stage, the student and supervisor must meet regularly to discuss progress and issues related to the topic of the thesis, and the supervisor is committed to providing the scientific department with a periodic report on the stages of completion. The thesis must demonstrate the student’s knowledge and familiarity with the relevant literature and the methodology. The thesis must also be accompanied by specific results and recommendations that are applicable in practice. The form of the thesis must comply with the regulations stated in the Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines, issued by the College of Graduate Studies, and it must pass the stage of scrutiny and verification of the absence of plagiarism or scientific theft through certain programs, including Turnitin. After completing writing it, it will be discussed in a public session by a specialized committee that includes an external examiner and an internal examiner headed by the supervisor.

courses.title: World Trade Agreements (E)
courses.description: This course examines the multilateral and regional legal regimes governing importation and exportation of goods across national borders. Key topics include the history and institutions of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and World Trade Organization (WTO), accession to the WTO, dispute settlement under WTO rules, transparency and participation in the GATT-WTO system, regulation of import duties and non-tariff barriers, rules on customs classification and valuation.

courses.title: E-Commerce ( E )
courses.description: This course addresses the legal regulation of e-commerce in the UAE in order to shed light on the strengths and weaknesses in the legislation of the UAE and explore the main challenges and prospects of modern e-commerce law. Therefore, this course deals with the following topics: the legal requirement of e-commerce, the electronic contract and its elements, electronic signature, the legislative framework for electronic authentication services, electronic consumer protection, the validity and evidential weight of e-mails and electronic records, and other related topics.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Private International Law
courses.description: The student studies an in-depth or comparative topic from the subjects of private international law in the field of judicial jurisdiction conflicts, conflicts of laws, enforcement of foreign judgments, the status of foreigners, nationality, or other related topics (such as the applicable law on international contracts, or the status of foreign law before the national judiciary).

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Civil Procedure
courses.description: The student studies in depth a topic of civil procedural law, such as the defense system, the adversarial system, the theory of rulings, the theory of appeal, the conflict between judicial rulings, or other topics. The course also includes an extensive discussion of formal and substantive defenses and judicial jurisdiction.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Insurance Contract
courses.description: This course includes studying the definition of insurance contract, identifying its characteristics, and distinguishing it from other named contracts. Its pillars are based on mutual consent and the subject matter that fundamentally involves risks. The course examines its effects by defining the obligations of the insured and the insurer. It also addresses the study of contractual models (insurance documents) in the insurance contract and how the insured is protected from arbitrary provisions therein as a consumer, especially since these models are unilaterally drafted by the insurer as the stronger party in the contractual relationship and the insured has no right to amend them. It explains and analyzes the levels of legal protection for the insured in terms of general contract theory and the judicial authorities concerning arbitrary contractual provisions in insurance contracts, considering the insured as a consumer and how to protect them according to this legal description, then in terms of decisions of the Higher Insurance Authority in Abu Dhabi and the extent to which the insured benefits from them. The course instructor selects a deep topic from these terms after covering an overview of all the course vocabulary in the first two weeks of the semester. For example, the instructor may choose the risk insured against, or discuss the terms of compensation in compulsory insurance, or address the topic of contingent rights in an insurance contract.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Intellectual Property
courses.description: This course deals with the protection and scope of copyright and related rights, patent rights, design rights, the rights of the designer of the layout designs of integrated circuits, the rights of the creator of plant varieties in national laws and international agreements such as the Berne Convention, TRIPS Agreement, and Paris Convention. This course also examines the obligations of the owners of these rights, the compulsory and optional licensing of these rights, and the duration of protection. Further, it discusses the role of some international organizations in regulating intellectual property rights and the legal issues arising in this regard along with their practical impact on sectors such as the pharmaceutical sector and the radio and television broadcasting sector. The course discusses also the collective management of copyright and its role in protecting copyright in the digital environment. Furthermore, the course covers trademarks, undisclosed information, and unfair competition. After providing a comprehensive overview of the above topics, the course professor focuses the course on discussing in depth one or more of these topics.

courses.title: Civil Law
courses.description: This course offers an in-depth study into one of the topics relating to civil law. It concentrates on the legal issues and problems from a practical and comparative perspective, and evaluates the legal recognition of the current civil contracts by addressing the main areas of strength or weakness in this regard and determining what the law ought to be in order to strike a balance between the different interests of the parties involved. Topics to be covered include: Duty to achieve a specific result; Duty of best efforts; personal guarantees and insurances in kind;. the liability arising from personal acts, the liability arising from the acts of others, Professional responsibility, compensation for moral damage, Joint ownership, insurance again liability, and so forth.

courses.title: Commercial law
courses.description: This course discuss one of the topics relating to Commercial Law according to its importance. It offers an in-depth study into one of the topics relating to commercial law. It concentrates on the legal issues and problems from a practical and comparative perspective, and evaluates the legal recognition of the current commercial contracts by addressing the main areas of strength or weakness in this regard and determining what the law ought to be in order to strike a balance between the different interests of the parties involved. Topics to be covered include: the theory of the merchant, the commercial activities, the banking operations, commercial competition, electronic commerce, and so forth.

courses.title: Civil Procedures Law - E
courses.description: This course shall examine deeply the process for advancing claims in the civil law context. It is essentially a course that will provide students with the framework for commencing a proceeding the civil court and/or responding to a claim that has been advanced. It will focus on examining the Rules of Civil Procedure, which will be augmented with a discussion of case law and how the rules have been interpreted.This course is based on writing researches and discussing issues relating to the rules governing the litigation process according to the UAE and Comparative laws. Topics in this course may include: judicial jurisdiction, parties to civil litigation, the theory of dispute, Judgment and the elements of reasoning, the defenses theory, the theory of appeal, and the effects of judicial decisions.

courses.title: Companies Law and Investment Legislation - E
courses.description: This course deals with the main provisions governing commercial companies in UAE, with special emphasis on the current areas of strength or weakness relating to the legal framework for doing business in UAE. Furthermore, this course sheds light on the legal recognition of free zones in the State and the role of the relevant institutions in attracting investments. By encouraging students to conduct presentations; discuss recent issues relating to companies and investment in the State, produce written work and collaborate with peers on set tasks or projects, this course will develop the ability of PhD students to delineate and evaluate issues, think analytically, select relevant materials and produce reasoned arguments encompassing policy, existing practice and knowledge.

courses.title: Real-Estate Legislation- E
courses.description: This course explores the legal regulation of real-estate transactions in the UAE by requiring students to present their own arguments, provide comments on the main judicial decisions, examine specific real estate contracts, and then present a written work on current real estate problems. This course also compares the local real-estate legislation followed in the United Arab Emirates with other legislation in some countries, and determines what the law ought to be in order to create a suitable and transparent investment climate that protects the rights of all involved parties. By doing so, this course provides a comparative perspective on real estate legal issues, and enhances the students’ ability of analyzing and reasoning using statutes, court rules and judicial opinions.

courses.title: Private International Law- E
courses.description: This course deals deeply with selected topics of Private International Law such as: the international jurisdiction of the courts, the applicable law to the disputes that contain a foreign element, the enforcement of foreign judgments, conflict of laws, and the disputes of nationality. Furthermore, this course focuses on the practical matters and integrates comparative and international perspectives on most issues. It also provides students with the required skills to construct research questions, and develop argumentation relating to the problems associated with the application of private international law rules with regard to jurisdiction, recognition of foreign judgments, and other topics of discussion.

courses.title: Securities and their Governing Legislation - E
courses.description: This course deeply examines the legal and regulatory framework applicable to the Securities markets in UAE. Students in this course will be encouraged to evaluate, research, and analyze the various aspects of securities regulation studied. Students will also be required to provide comments on the current practices and judicial decisions in this regard. Topics include: the main types of securities and the conditions and legal requirements for their issuance and trading; the rules of speculation in the financial markets, the liability of brokers and the mechanisms of investor protection; insider trading and stock market manipulation. Emphasis is also placed on the role of the Securities and Commodities Authority in controling the financial market.

courses.title: Advanced Arabic Language Skills for Law
courses.description: This course has two main objectives: First, to make law students aware of the importance of language, helping them understand that mastering it allows for precise legal expression and provides a correct understanding of legal texts. Second, to develop their speaking and linguistic abilities, enhancing their capacity to analyze and communicate legal discourse effectively. Therefore, the course is divided into four units: Grammar, Analytical Reading, Legal Writing, and Speaking. The first unit (Grammar) aims to ensure students master key grammatical concepts based on their high school studies, with an emphasis on essential grammar rules. The second unit (Analytical Reading) is designed to teach students how to read legal texts accurately and analyze them linguistically and semantically, facilitating correct understanding and interpretation. The third unit (Legal Writing) focuses on training students to write legally precise texts, free of grammatical and stylistic errors, and to practice writing on topics relevant to their studies in law school. The fourth unit (Speaking) aims to equip students with the skills for effective legal delivery and the correct oral presentation of legal texts.

courses.title: Legal Research Methodology
courses.description: This course is divided into two parts, the first one is theoretical, and the second one is practical. In the first part, the instructor provides the student with the necessary knowledge to write a research based on scientific standards, by explaining the various levels and types of legal scientific research, scientific resources and tools, and how to systematically combine and organize these resources. In addition to, explaining how to choose a research topic and research methods in the legal field and how to develop a research plan. Then, to provide basic guidelines on legal writing, and documentation of resources, and ethics to be adhered by the scholar. Whereas, in the second part the student is asked to write a research and apply the theorical knowledge of legal research methodology under the supervision of the instructor.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT113 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT113 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: English Legal Terminology
courses.description: This course provides students with the meaning and use of a wide range of legal English vocabulary and phrases used in fundamental areas of law. Through the examination of key law paragraphs, principles, and themes, the course provides an interactive learning style to enhance students' ability to read and understand legal texts and vocabulary in the English language.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT213 with a minimum grade D; PRVT227 with a minimum grade D; PUBL215 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT213 with a minimum grade D
PRVT227 with a minimum grade D
PUBL215 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Selected Studies in Comparative Law (E)
courses.description: This course introduces students to legal concepts, principles and procedures of comparative law. The course provides students with a broad understanding of the different legal systems which exist globally; their historical backgrounds; sources of law and major legal institutions. It also considers selected topics in private law, such as the formation of contract, Arbitration, and the main types of companies. On the other hand, this course includes the study of some selected areas of public law, i.e. International Law, Administrative Law, Constitutional Law, and Criminal Law.
courses.prerequisiteText: LAW228 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: LAW228 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Training 1
courses.description: The course provides training for students on performing the basic tasks carried out by legal professionals in practice. It involves training in researching legal rules necessary for addressing real-world problems. It also involves training in exercising legal expression both in writing and orally, through writing various legal documents such as memoranda of legal opinion, statements of claims, defence memos, judicial decisions and contracts, in addition to oral pleadings. Students are also provided with the values that a legal professional must adhere to when practicing his profession. Furthermore, the course includes organizing practical field visits to training bodies such as courts, public prosecution offices, international law firms, and arbitration centres, and hosting several professional experts from these institutions.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Law
courses.description: This course aims to study the legal and ethical implications of the use of artificial intelligence in various areas of life. This includes private relationships: i.e., its impact on contract formation and execution, intellectual property rights, tort liability, and dispute resolution through the judiciary and alternative methods. It also covers aspects of public law, particularly in the areas of criminalization, punishment, and criminal procedures, as well as constitutional rights, privacy, and the impact of AI on public administration governance. The course places special emphasis on practical applications in both national and comparative judicial systems.

courses.title: Training 2
courses.description: The course of external training aims to provide the student of the College of Law with the proper legal training at those institutions that are involved, at different levels, in the application of the law. Its objective is to reinforce the students’ theoretical and practical knowledge which were gained throughout their studies in the classes. The course also seeks to familiarize students with the work environment and the processes implemented in the judiciary, in specific, and other legal institutions, in general. (The course is conducted over 6 weeks in any of last year semesters (including Summer). No courses are allowed to be registered during the internship).

courses.title: Legal Research
courses.description: This course revolves around the fundamentals of legal research in terms of the concept of legal research, its levels and types, methodologies, sources and tools for collecting scientific material, and the principles of legal writing. It also covers the ethics of scientific research in the field of law and how to practice proper oral expression linked to research activity at all stages. Based on the foregoing, the student is tasked with preparing one legal research paper ranging between 15 and 25 pages, and performing an oral presentation of the various stages of the research activity starting from selecting the research topic to the final presentation of it.

courses.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Research Methods
courses.description: The course covers the study of various scientific research methods, particularly quantitative and qualitative research methods, the design of research plans, and the process of conducting scientific research using a wide variety of relevant primary and secondary research sources and techniques. The course also focuses on the principles, skills, and methods necessary for conducting legal research, including the selection of the research sample, data and doctrinal analysis, theory building and testing, and case study.

courses.title: Advanced Legal Research: Writing and Presentation
courses.description: The couse provides a definition of scientific research in the field of law, its types and and levels, selection of the subject of research, methods of legal research, legal writing, research ethics and refernce documentation. As a course requirement, the student must write a legal research paper which reflects commitment to the relevant ethical and prpfessional rules in the fiels of law.

courses.title: Selected Legal Readings - E
courses.description: This course will provide students with an overview of legal concepts, procedures, terminology and current issues in law including international law, administrative law, Commercial law, Contract law, employment law and so forth. By reading about selected topics in law, this course will also develop the ability of PhD students to delineate and evaluate issues, think analytically, select relevant materials and produce reasoned arguments encompassing policy, existing practice and knowledge. There is no one single book which covers the whole subject area. Students will be exposed to various sources of English scholarly materials including textbooks, websites, databases and law journals that are relevant to the selected themes raised by the instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Comparative Legal Systems
courses.description: Since many of the research projects will necessarily involve some study of materials from other legal systems, a minimum level of familiarity with other legal systems would be necessary. This course is designed to introduce students to the theory and practice of comparative law by providing them with a broad understanding of the different major legal systems which exist globally; their historical backgrounds; their sources and characteristics. The course also considers selected topics in private or public law, looking at how different legal systems respond to issues familiar to students from studies within their own legal disciplines. During the course, students will be given the opportunity to compare specific areas of law between various jurisdictions. They may also explore some distinguishing features of Common and Civil Law. Topics to be covered in this course shall include for example the doctrine of judicial precedent and its use in the different legal systems, the role of judge and jury in common law system, and the theory of contract under the different major legal systems.

courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: The comprehensive examination, which is an integral part of the PhD Program, is designed to ascertain and assess the student's comprehensive and in-depth knowledge of the main areas in the field of law and to evaluate the student’s potential to complete a doctoral dissertation successfully. Students who pass the comprehensive examination may advance to Ph.D. Dissertation. In preparation for the comprehensive examination, the student is required to develop a specific area of interest that shall be approved by the College Council. The specific area of interest will be articulated in the student’s statement of interest which ought to be submitted with the application to the program. The specific area of interest is expected to be the subject of the student’s dissertation.
courses.corequisiteText: LAW703 with a minimum grade C; ( PRVT711 with a minimum grade C or PUBL715 with a minimum grade C)
corequisiteItems: LAW703 with a minimum grade C
( PRVT711 with a minimum grade C or PUBL715 with a minimum grade C)

courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Student conducts high quality academic research under the direction of his/her supervisor. Student and supervisor shall meet on regular basis and discuss progress and issues related to the student’s dissertation research. Furthermore, the student writes an annual report based on a meeting with supervisor and Advisory Committee, in which a review is conducted to determine progress, identify problems, and project dates for completion of various tasks. The research shall represent original contribution to human knowledge in the particular field of law and is presented in a written research dissertation of a publishable standard. The document shall also demonstrate the candidate’s acquaintance with the literature of the field and the proper selection and execution of research methodology. The dissertation shall not exceed 70000 words in length. The physical form of the dissertation must comply with the regulations stated in the Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines, issued by the College of Graduate Studies.
courses.prerequisiteText: LAW702 with a minimum grade C
prerequisiteItems: LAW702 with a minimum grade C

courses.title: Introduction to Islamic Law and its Sources
courses.description: The course deals with an introduction to the definition of jurisprudence and Sharia, its divisions and the characteristics. The role of Islamic jurisprudence is covered through the study of its various sources, like The Quran, The Sunna, Fiqh consensus, inference, open interests, approbation, pretext closure accompanying and Tradition.
courses.prerequisiteText: GELW111 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: GELW111 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Constitutional Law
courses.description: This course contains a brief study of the 'State', elements of State, forms of State and powers of State in comparative systems, with special focus on the Federal State and its application in the UAE. The main focus would be on the study of Constitutional Law, its definition, its sources, the control on the constitutional validity of laws and application of these aspects in the UAE. The course also deals with a study of the Constitutional Organization of the Federal Authorities according to the UAE Constitution.
courses.prerequisiteText: GELW111 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: GELW111 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Administrative Law
courses.description: The course covers the definition and sources of Administrative law, and the activities of the public administration, i.e., execution of laws, preservation of public order, and public utilities. The course focuses also on various legal means of public administration: administrative decisions, administrative contracts and public property.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT113 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT113 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Public International Law
courses.description: The course includes the definition of Public International Law, its sources subjects. The inter-relation between the Domestic Law (Municipal Law) and Public International Law and the governing theories are adequately dealt with. Various aspects covering Public International Law in times of peace are also dealt with, including, the Law of Treaties, establishment of States- their rights and obligations, recognition, state responsibility, use of force, and settlement of international disputes.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT113 with a minimum grade D; PUBL114 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT113 with a minimum grade D
PUBL114 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: General Law of Crimes and Penalties (1)
courses.description: The course includes a general introduction to the study of criminal law, specifically the general part and the general theory of crime. The study covers the characteristics of the general part of criminal law, its relationship with other legal and criminal sciences, and its scope of application in terms of time and place. It also includes the study of the general elements of a crime: the material and moral elements, the provisions of criminal participation, justifications, and grounds for exemption from criminal liability. Additionally, the course addresses the latest technological developments and their impact on some of its topics, such as the possibility of establishing criminal liability resulting from using artificial intelligence applications and the newly introduced penalties that could be applied if such liability is recognized.
courses.prerequisiteText: PRVT113 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PRVT113 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: General Law of Crimes and Penalties (2)
courses.description: The course includes the study of the general theory of criminal sanctions, focusing on two main areas. The first area is the General Theory of Punishment, which covers the definition of punishment, its characteristics, and how it differs from other legal sanctions. It also explores the various types of punishments, the rules governing their application, and the discretionary powers of the criminal judge in this regard. The second area is the General Theory of Non-Punitive Measures, which examines the definition and characteristics of non-punitive measures, their distinction from punishment, the different types of non-punitive measures, and their scope of application. Additionally, the course addresses the issue of various criminal sanctions that may be imposed for responsibility related to offences committed through AI.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL215 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL215 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Environmental Policy and Climate Justice
courses.description: The objective of the course is to provide students with working knowledge of legal norms and practices that address contemporary environmental issues. It focuses on UAE laws, Acts, regulations and, familiarizing students with key international legal concepts by studying major conventions and treaties. In addition to legal frameworks, the course explores the intersection of environmental law with policy making and climate justice, emphasizing how laws can shape fair and sustainable outcomes for vulnerable communities. It underlines the crucial links between environmental protection, socio-economic development, sustainability, and the global pursuit of climate equity.

courses.title: Criminal Law and Penalties – Special Part
courses.description: The Special Section of the Criminal Law (Penal Code) Course addresses the detailed and special provisions for some crimes. The study of this Course is divided into two parts: the first includes the study of crimes against persons, which are intentional and unintentional homicide and assault. The second includes studying crimes against money, which are crimes of theft, fraud, and breach of trust. The course discusses the effect of the use of new technologies on these topics, including the issue of responsibility for offences committed through AI applications and different criminal sanctions that may be imposed in such cases.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL216 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL216 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Penal Law (Specific) 2 "Emerging Crimes"
courses.description: This course deals with particular types of crimes: offences against the public interest, economic crimes, information technology crimes, drug crimes, money laundering, and human trafficking. A cohernet set of offences contained in the vocabulary of this course is to be chosen and taught in each semester.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL209 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL209 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: International Organizations-English
courses.description: The course studies the idea of international organizations and their general rules, membership in international organizations, the organs and staff of international organizations, the functions and powers of international organizations, the international legal personality of international organizations, and their decision-making process. The course also covers international organizations such as the League of Nations, and GCC, the United Nations, and some regional and specialized organizations.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL207 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL207 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Public Employment
courses.description: It includes: studying the legal provisions for the public employee in terms of his public service and his or her rights and obligations and his disciplin in accordance to the Federal Civil Service Act and its implemented regulations in United Arab Emirates.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL206 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL206 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Public Finance and Tax Legislation
courses.description: This course covers two main topics. The first is the Science of Public Finance, which explores the principles, rules, and theories governing state finances. This area consists of three key elements: public expenditures, public revenues, and the public budget. Public revenues include taxes, state-owned properties, fees, and public loans. The second topic is Tax Legislation, which focuses on the legal provisions related to taxation in the United Arab Emirates, with particular emphasis on value-added tax (VAT) and excise tax.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL206 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL206 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Principles of Jurisprudence
courses.description: In this course, the student becomes familiar with the concept of the science of Usul al-Fiqh, its subject matter, benefits, sources, origins, and schools. The course also introduces the theory of the Islamic legal ruling, including the lawgiver, the ruling in its two categories—obligatory (taklifi) and declaratory (wadi‘)—as well as the subject of the ruling and the person to whom it applies. Furthermore, the student explores the discussions on semantic indications according to the jurists, including: types of clear expressions—zahir (apparent), nass (explicit), mufassar (elucidated), and muhkam (unequivocal); types of ambiguous expressions—khafi (latent), mushkil (problematic), mujmal (general), and mutashabih (equivocal); types of expressions based on the assignment of meaning—‘amm (general) and its specification, and khas (specific) and its categories such as command and prohibition, absolute and restricted, and homonymous; types of expressions based on their usage—literal and figurative, explicit and implicit; and types of expressions based on how they signify meaning—through explicit wording, indication, implication, presumption, and the concept of opposition.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL112 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL112 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Criminal Procedures Law
courses.description: The course covers the following topics: the scope of application of the Criminal Procedure Law in terms of time and place, criminal cases arising from crimes, evidence collection, preliminary investigation, trial, sentencing, appeal, and special criminal procedures (criminal reconciliation - criminal mediation - criminal settlement - electronic monitoring - use of technologies in criminal procedures). The course also addresses the legitimacy of the use of new technologies, including AI, in criminal procedures.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL216 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL216 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: International Law of the Sea
courses.description: The Course studies the following Topics: The Foundation of the International Law of the Sea and its development, Internal Waters, Territorial Sea, Contiguous Zone, Exclusive Economic Zone, Continental Shelf, The Legal Status of High Seas, International Straits and, Disputes Settlement Mechanisms in the International Law of Sea. Also, it analysis Federal Law no. (19) of 1993 on the Delimitation of Maritime Zones in the UAE.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL207 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL207 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: International Human Rights Law
courses.description: The course studies the theory oh human rights, its deveploment in the positive international law, particularly in the United Nations system and in the international and regional human rights conventions. It deals also with the international mechanisms for the protection of human rights and it focusses on the jurisdiction of the european court of human rights. In addition, the course will deal with the international mechanism available for individualsincluding the individual complaint, and with the application of human rights conventions in the domestic legal systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: PUBL207 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: PUBL207 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Press Law and Ethics
courses.description: This course includes two parts. Part I is dedicated to a brief study of the ethics prescribed by the codes of ethics that deal with the different aspects of conduct of persons who are working in the fields of mass media. Part II contains a brief study about the main elements of the Mass Media Legal System in the world in general, and a focused study of the legal system of mass media in the UAE (print and electronic media/journalism and cinema) in particular. The Mass Media Legal system in the UAE, their establishment, administration, activities and the related legal issues like restraints, prohibitions on the freedom of expression involving criminal and administrative procedures are part of this course.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Criminal Law and Penalties
courses.description: This course concentrates on 2 different topics in the criminal law (general principles). The first topic deals with one of the crime elements and the second topic will concentrate on the theory of punishment and related theories. Examples of these topics are the study of the act of actus reus and mens rea of the crime, and the custodian institutions.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Constitutional Law
courses.description: This course focuses on the study of a topic within constitutional law, with consideration given to topics relevant to the United Arab Emirates. The study will be conducted in depth and will involve comparisons with various legal systems that either provide distinct or similar regulations to the subject matter. Additionally, several lectures will be dedicated to reviewing the general principles of constitutional law, as they are essential for comprehending the subject matter and engaging in profound study.

courses.title: Advance Studies in International Criminal Law
courses.description: This course provides introduction to international criminal law, its historical development with emphasis on the establishment of the International Criminal Tribunal. The study of the International Criminal Tribunal focuses on its jurisdiction, applicable procedures, pre-trial and trial process on international level.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Criminal Procedures
courses.description: This course examines one or more topics in Criminal Procedure Law that hold practical significance and present application challenges. The course offers an in-depth and comparative study of these topics from jurisprudential and judicial perspectives. For example, alternatives to criminal proceedings, such as criminal orders, criminal reconciliation, and criminal settlements, as well as The Theory of Criminal Evidence, methods of appealing criminal judgments, including opposition, appeal, and cassation. The course also covers using new technologies, including AI, in criminal Procedures.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Administrative Law
courses.description: This course focuses on studying one of the topics of administrative law that concerns the United Arab Emirates, with the necessity of conducting an in-depth study and comparison with some systems that provide different or similar regulations for this subject. It is also considered important to allocate a number of lectures to review the general principles of administrative law as they are essential for understanding the specific subject under deep study.

courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: The student is committed to conduct original research on a vital topic of private law under the supervision of his or her academic supervisor, which will be presented in the form of a thesis written according to a publishable standard. The writing stage must be preceded by holding a seminar for the student to discuss the topic of the thesis with the relevant faculty members in a public session. During the writing stage, the student and supervisor must meet regularly to discuss progress and issues related to the topic of the thesis, and the supervisor is committed to providing the scientific department with a periodic report on the stages of completion. The thesis must demonstrate the student’s knowledge and familiarity with the relevant literature and the methodology. The thesis must also be accompanied by specific results and recommendations that are applicable in practice. The form of the thesis must comply with the regulations stated in the Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines, issued by the College of Graduate Studies, and it must pass the stage of scrutiny and verification of the absence of plagiarism or scientific theft through certain programs, including Turnitin. After completing writing it, it will be discussed in a public session by a specialized committee that includes an external examiner and an internal examiner headed by the supervisor.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Administrative Contracts
courses.description: In this course, the student studies a topic related to administrative contracts pertinent to the current situation in the United Arab Emirates. The chosen topic should have practical implications and be studied in-depth, with comparisons to the provisions of comparative law. Several lectures will be dedicated to reviewing general rules and basic concepts of administrative contracts, considering their importance in understanding the subject matter for in-depth study.

courses.title: International Relations & Organizations(E)
courses.description: This course includes the study of the governmental international organizations and their role in the maintenance of international peace and security, and focusing on the legality of the use of force in international relations. The course deals in details with the following concepts: use of military force in the United Nations Charter, Self Defense , Pre-emptive military strikes, Humanitarian Intervention and military strikes against non -states entities.

courses.title: Human Rights (E)
courses.description: The Course includes the study of Human Rights Theory and its application through the study of Human Rights Conventions, Governmental International Organizations and the relationship between International human rights law and Domestic legal systems. The Course includes the study of: Human Rights, the cultural aspects of human rights, civil and political rights, economic, social and cultural rights and the human rights protection mechanisms.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Special Criminal Legislation
courses.description: The course includes an in-depth study of one or two crimes covered under special penal laws, as well as emerging crimes such as drug crimes, cybercrimes, money laundering, and human trafficking. It focuses particularly on newly emerging crimes resulting from advancements in technology—especially artificial intelligence—and crimes related to personal data and the human genome.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Pre-trial Procedures
courses.description: This unit examines the institutions and criminal processes involved in pre-trial stages. It covers preliminary police criminal investigations and procedures such as police power and authority to stop, search and arrest suspects. It also covers evidence gathering by police, preserving crimes scenes, the accused and victims’ rights before judicial police, and other related police powers during this stage. It will also explore the various criminal procedures of primary criminal investigation as conducted by public prosecutors such as interrogation, detention, bail, committal proceedings and the prosecutor decision of there is no grounds to file a lawsuit. The unit also deals with the various aspects of the criminal evidence theory.

courses.title: Environmental Law
courses.description: The course is designed to develop working knowledge of legal norms and practices that apply to the environment. Students will have an opportunity to apply this knowledge to case studies to illustrate how environmental law applies in real situations. The course incorporates on-line use of current Acts, Regulations and Conventions and students will become familiar with Municipal, Federal and international environmental law including duty, breach and liability.

courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.description: The course deals with one or more topics of substantive or procedural criminal law in an in-depth manner, taking into consideration the modern aspects related to the UAE, such as the evolution of the criminal responsibility of legal persons, the principle of the judge's freedom of conviction or the crimes of human trafficking.

courses.title: Administrative Law
courses.description: This course offers an in-depth study into one of the Administrative law topics. Its purpose is to advance of students’ comprehension of the different topics of Administrative law. The Course will focus on one or more substantive or procedural issues which is selected by the Department of Public law in each Semester , with focus on contemporary questions of the UAE Administrative law.

courses.title: Public International Law - E
courses.description: This course aims to study one of the public international law topics in depth, such as state immunity, international inheritance and unilateral acts in international law. - State immunity: Talks about the concepts of state immunity, historical development and study of the United Nations Convention on state immunity and it’s applications in international and national courts. - International Inheritance: Talks about the concept of international inheritance, types and forms, and the succession of States in the light of international treaties and concentrates on the records, properties, debts and the declaration of the United Nations on succession of States in respect of nationality of natural persons and the problems raised by the issue of succession of states. - Unilateral acts: Talks about the concept of unilateral acts and it’s relation to the theory of the sources of international law: the legal forms and sequel.

courses.title: Criminal Procedure Law- E
courses.description: The course instructor will select one or more topics from the Code of Criminal Procedure that raise issues in jurisprudential theory and judicial application, ensuring that the study is in-depth and utilizes comparison to other laws and Islamic law.

courses.title: International Crimes and Judicial System - E
courses.description: The Course depends on requiring students to prepare papers, comment on judicial rulings in different subjects and holding discussion sessions on different topics related to the principles that govern the concept of international crimes and international judicial system. The Course will examine the elements and the development of war crimes, the crime of genocide, crimes against humanity, with special reference to the Statute of International Criminal Court, and ad hoc international criminal courts.

courses.title: Constitutional Law - E
courses.description: The Course boosts students academic capacity to write papers, comments on judicial rulings, and hold discussion sessions on variouse aspects of constitutional law , such as: the supremacy of constitution , political oversight over the constitutionality of laws and its development in France, the emergence of judicial review of constitutionality of laws in the United States, legal systems of judicial review, judicial review over the constitutionality of laws and its impact on the protection of rights and freedoms. It focuses on judicial review system in the UAE.

courses.title: Contemporary Crimes- E
courses.description: This Course will be concerned with preparing papers, commenting on judicial decisions and holding discussion sessions on one or more of the new crimes such as terrorism, crimes related to capital markets, Cyber-crimes, money laundering, and human trafficking.

courses.title: Human Gross Anatomy
courses.description: The structure of the human body will be studied in lectures and cadavers. The relationship between structure and function will be emphasized, as well as common variations which may or may not lead to altered function. In addition, the embryological processes leading to the gross structure, as well as the histological organization will be pointed out.

courses.title: Principles of Research
courses.description: The Principles of Research will offer MSC/PhD students the generic skills and methods they need to successfully complete their programs. The Principles of Research will use lectures, seminars and workshops and group discussions to introduce students to the methods for identifying, solving, analyzing and reporting of a specific problem pertinent to biomedical sciences. Laboratory data management and safety (environmental safety, radiation safety, and biosafety) will also be covered. At the end of the course, student will be able to select their bibliographical data from relevant databases, formulate a research hypothesis, design a research project, analyze and interpret data, write an abstract and a research manuscript and present a conference paper

courses.title: Techniques in Biochemistry
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to a range of experimental techniques that are in routine use in a functioning biochemistry laboratory with the objective that they can understand basic principles behind these techniques and are able to understand their applicability in their future research. Whenever possible, the course combines lectures illustrating the scientific principles underlying a particular technique with the demonstration of the methodology in the laboratory.

courses.title: Advanced Molecular Biology
courses.description: The field of Molecular and Cellular Biology has given scientists unprecedented control over species manipulation and development. This course will have an in-depth coverage of the structure, function, and synthesis of DNA, RNA, and proteins. In this course, we will discuss the nature of genes and chromosomes (the repositories of genetic information) and the mechanics of DNA synthesis and genome replication, followed by discussions on repair, recombination and transposition. We will also discuss the pathways of gene expression (transcription, RNA processing, and translation) and the mechanisms of regulating these pathways, with special emphasis on transcriptional control. Latest literature on these topics will be covered.

courses.title: Advanced Cell Biology
courses.description: This course will focus on the cellular biochemistry of higher organisms: mechanisms of cellular communication, intracellular signaling, cell growth and oncogenic transformation. During the course, two basic cellular structures will be discussed: membrane and mitochondria, two important key players in cell signaling and cell death. Concepts like cell signaling, cell cycle, oxidative stress and cell death will be reviewed. The course will end with an introductory lecture on stem cell biology. Recent experimental findings and new approaches used to investigate how cells work will be emphasized. Students will also be taught how to explore the cell biology literature and to critically evaluate scientific publications in some of the topics.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Biochemistry
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare students in learning advanced cellular biochemistry and metabolism under physiological and pathophysiological conditions for successful careers in academia and biotechnology industries. The course also provides enhanced education opportunities for students who wish to extend their knowledge, experience, and opportunities as independent scientists in academic research at universities, biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries, health/biomedical science management or teaching. In this course, advanced cellular biochemistry will be explained to signify the importance of metabolism in normal physiology and pathophysiological conditions. Faculty lectures and students reports will focus on these.

courses.title: Special topics in Biochemistry
courses.description: This course will provide students the chance to rotate through the laboratory of a potential supervisor to learn about the various projects in progress in that laboratory with emphasis on acquainting themselves with the type of research work and techniques being used. Regular attendance (one hour per week) and active participation of the student in observing and learning about these projects is of great importance. The students should study the literature provided by their respective supervisors and familiarize themselves with the research activities being carried out in the laboratory chosen by them.

courses.title: Recent Advances in Molecular Biology
courses.description: The field of Molecular and Cellular Biology has given scientists unprecedented control over species manipulation and development. This course will have an in-depth coverage of the structure, function, and synthesis of DNA, RNA, and proteins. We will discuss the nature of genes and chromosomes (the repositories of genetic information) and the mechanics of DNA synthesis and genome replication, followed by discussions on repair, recombination and transposition. We will also discuss the pathways of gene expression (transcription, RNA processing, and translation) and the mechanisms of regulating these pathways, with special emphasis on transcriptional control.

courses.title: Advanced Research Techniques
courses.description: This course aims to give a broad but comprehensive introduction to the majority of the important techniques used today in biomedical research. It aims to give a background in the theory, practise and applications of the various techniques, as well as their limitations and pitfalls. It is hoped that, after having completed the course, students will be well equipped to embark upon research projects with a useful knowledge of the techniques covered and how to apply them to address specific research-based questions, and also how to interpret the data derived from these applications. It is not the aim of the course to teach students how to perform various procedures - this can only be achieved with extensive, repeated, supervised, hands-on laboratory training which is obviously not feasible in this context. The format of each session may vary according to the individual needs of each topic or presenter. Most session will commence with a tutorial covering the principles and practice of the technique at hand, followed by a less formal session where instrumentation can be seen in operation, experimental examples can be examined, and raw data can be viewed and discussed.

courses.title: Advances in General Pathology
courses.description: The course is mainly General histopathology, which deals with the basic concept of the various disease processes. This program offers the students a comprehensive review of the theoretical and practical aspects of general histopathology. The students will be exposed to formal lectures and laboratory practicals, which will emphasize the most modern concepts and methodologies in the fields of cell injury, inflammation, tissue repair, infection, hemodynamic changes, vascular disorders, environmental disorders and neoplasia.

courses.title: Microbial Pathogenesis and Host Defense
courses.description: This course will explore ways in which microbial pathogens, particularly bacteria and viruses, interact with their hosts. Topics that will be covered include bacterial-host cell interactions, role of bacterial toxins in pathogenicity, viral infections and escape strategies, emerging and re-emerging viral infections, host defense and innate/adaptive immunity, exaggerated immune responses and immunopathology, virus-host cell interactions in cancerogenesis, and strategies for vaccine development.

courses.title: Current Advances in Pharmacological Sciences
courses.description: Pharmacology is an interdisciplinary field. This PhD course tackles major recent findings in divers’ area of pharmacology with a focus on cancer pharmacology, neurodegeneration and cognitive functions, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. This course emphasis is on the molecular mechanism of action of the most recent applied and experimental drugs including monoclonal antibodies, tissue engineering advances, and genome editing progress. Therefore, the contents of the course will remain dynamic and evolve from year to year depending on what is viewed as significant advances in that year. It is intended that the seminar should provide a more didactic and interactive meeting. During this course, students will also be introduced to the most advanced research methodologies and will have extensive training to develop their skills, including ethics and communication that will be achieved via written assessments and oral presentations and discussions.

courses.title: Advances in Genetics
courses.description: This course is designed to cover selected topics and recently published articles that are influencing in a significant manner our understanding of human genetics and genomics with emphasis on recent advances in genomic technologies and disease mechanisms. Therefore, the contents of the course might vary from year to year depending on what is viewed as a significant advance in that year.

courses.title: Advanced Cancer Biology
courses.description: This course will focus on cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying cancer progression, metastasis, and recurrence. Advances in cancer treatment, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy will also be discussed. This course will be based around seminars and interactive discussion sessions focused on the latest developments in the field accompanied by critical evaluation of published research articles. The content of the course will evolve from year to year depending on the latest advances in the field. During the interactive group sessions, there will be a round table discussion of selected research papers (which will be pre-circulated to all students) concerning important topics in cancer. The students will learn to dissect the study’s major aims, methodology and logic employed to address the question, the strengths and weaknesses of the results, and their implications. The emphasis will be on the methodological, conceptual and practical aspects of the research papers in the field. An important part of this course will be to develop the student’s ability to critically evaluate published research papers. The manuscript for evaluation will be selected by the course coordinators and provided to each student at the beginning of the course. In consultation with the course coordinator and co-coordinator, each student will also select a research paper/topic and prepare it for presentation to the whole class at the end of the course.

courses.title: Medical Cell and Tissue Biology
courses.description: This course will guide students in learning advanced information on the microscopic structure of the cells and tissues of the human body and the biological features of their components. The correlation of structure and function at the cellular and molecular levels will be emphasized in lectures and laboratory sessions. The application of cell and tissue biology to research and clinical disciplines will be emphasized. For each topic, an introduction to the cellular architecture and specialized function of a given tissue will provide the necessary background that will explore contemporary research into the molecular and cellular basis of human diseases involving that tissue.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Neuroscience
courses.description: Advanced Topics in Neuroscience is a course that focuses on specific contents that are particularly relevant to modern neuroscience and pathophysiology of the nervous system, allowing students to discuss, critique, and interpret primary research literature in the field. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to demonstrate comprehensive and integrated knowledge at the frontier of this discipline and explain critically the highly complex and diverse matters in this field. In addition, the course will explore training and practice on translational idea generation and refinement. It is a modular course that provides broad base to sample contemporary understanding and developments on normal and abnormal brain functioning, allowing each student to focus on selected topic of interest. The course will focus on specific contents that are especially relevant to gain a deeper understanding of ourselves, how the nervous system works and what controls our behaviors, including consciousness learning and memory, brain plasticity, and motor functions. However, it also covers the most recent developments in the neurobiology of diseases, including neurodegeneration, movement disorders, autism, depression, stress related diseases and other neurological and psychiatric diseases. The course will also cover principles of the most recent cutting-edge technologies available to study brain function like connectomics, super-resolution microscopy, functional MRI, EEG, electrophysiology and calcium imaging. The course is composed of weekly seminar series in which various topics about modern neuroscience are discussed. Seminars are also presented by students or when suitable by visiting outside neuroscientists. At the end of the course, student will submit a reflection paper on a chosen topic of special interest/thesis relevance. The reflection paper can be structured as a literature synthesis, opinion paper, theoretical paper, or a research grant proposal. Together, the seminars and reflection paper will prepare the student for the course assessment during which the candidate will be examined on deep comprehension and critical thinking of a broader research topic/paper.

courses.title: Advanced Pathophysiology
courses.description: Pathophysiology identifies the changes that occur when a function of the body is compromised by disease, injury or other abnormality. In Advanced Pathophysiology course students will explore the application of advanced knowledge of the complex physiological functions and pathophysiological processes to understand the fundamental mechanisms of organ health and disease. The course will be focusing on pathophysiology of three bodily systems, including the cardiovascular, respiratory and gastrointestinal system as major focus points of research in the department. Selected topics from other bodily systems will also be explored. The course will enable students to discuss, critique, interpret and eventually contrast primary research literature in each and between those fields. At the end of the course students will be able to demonstrate comprehensive and integrated knowledge at the frontier of pathophysiology and explain critically the highly complex and diverse matters in this field. The course has modular structure with up 30% of the topics modifiable aiming to provide broad yet targeted knowledge and understanding of abnormal bodily functioning. Particular attention is given to the most recent cutting-edge technologies available to examine the alterations in function as well as adaptive, integrative and regulatory mechanisms of bodily dysfunction at the molecular, cellular, organ and system levels. The course combines seminars, lectures and presentations, and focused integration sessions led by students and faculty. At the end of the course, students will have to submit a reflection paper on a chosen topic of special interest/thesis relevance. The reflection paper can be structured as a literature synthesis, opinion paper, theoretical paper, or a research grant proposal. Finally, the course will insert a small focused discussion, training and practice on translational idea generation and refinement; here the main emphasis will be on comparative research of underlying pathophysiological processes across bodily systems. At the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate deep comprehension and critical thinking of a pathophysiologic processes.

courses.title: Computational Biochemistry and Artificial Intelligence for Medical Applications
courses.description: Computational sciences and artificial intelligence have been integrated in ubiquitous applications in the fields of sciences and medicine. This technology serves as a powerful tool to mark advancements in research, discoveries and medical practice. This course is composed of two parts: Computational Biochemistry and Artificial Intelligence. The first part covers computational sciences with focus on molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and quantum mechanics. It is a combination of theory and computational practical sessions. The theory will include the fundamentals and limitations of each of the methods, and the practical sessions will involve hands-on applications on chemical or biochemical systems. The second part covers artificial intelligence and its applications. It includes the fundamentals of statistics and machine learning algorithms. The theory of this part will be complemented by hands-on sessions that involve model building, technique validation and decision analysis, with focus on medical applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM113 with a minimum grade D; BIOC160 with a minimum grade D
prerequisiteItems: CHEM113 with a minimum grade D
BIOC160 with a minimum grade D

courses.title: Advanced Human Microbiome
courses.description: The microbiome is the genomic content of all microorganisms (microbiota) inhabiting different parts of the human body. Alterations in microbiome composition have been associated with many diseases including inflammatory bowel disease, autoimmune diseases, cancers and diabetes. Multi-omics techniques, including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses, are used to better understand how the microbiota are acting on and interacting with the hosts in health and disease. This course will provide the students with deep understanding of microbial communities causing different types of diseases, their diversity, interaction with the immune system, modulation and impact on human health. Students will be exposed to modern molecular techniques and bioinformatics tools for profiling and analyzing microbiome data. They will also learn how to integrate these data to develop a holistic understanding of the interactions between host and microbial communities in both health and disease states.
courses.prerequisiteText: MMIM601 or MMIM602 or

courses.title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Virology
courses.description: Virology is a dynamic and rapidly evolving field. This course is tailored for PhD students seeking to deepen their understanding of cutting-edge developments in virology, and to explore the intricate molecular and cellular mechanisms governing viral infections and associated diseases. The course will provide an in-depth examination of the latest breakthroughs and methodologies in virology research, encompassing a diverse range of topics, including viral entry and replication, host-pathogen interactions, immune evasion strategies, oncogenic viruses and antiviral therapies. Additionally, students will learn how to identify potential areas of novel research, how to write a seed grant and identify appropriate funding bodies.
courses.prerequisiteText: MMIM603 or BMB602 or MMIM602 or BMB603 or BMSC700
prerequisiteItems: MMIM603 or BMB602 or MMIM602 or BMB603 or BMSC700

courses.title: Advanced Immunology
courses.description: The field of immunology has witnessed a huge surge in knowledge over the past 50 years, becoming one of the most dynamic and exciting areas of medical sciences. Dysregulated immune reactions are the basis of many human diseases, including cancer, inflammation, autoimmunity, allergy, neurodegeneration and immunodeficiencies. The Advanced Immunology course provides an intensive and in‐depth examination of fundamental concepts in immunology, including (1) the interplay between innate and adaptive immune systems; (2) function of immune regulatory circuits; and (3) immunopathogenesis of selected human diseases. Our improved understanding of the immune system has provided the foundation for the development of new modalities for treating chronic diseases such as cancer, autoimmunity and autoinflammatory disorders.
courses.prerequisiteText: MMIM601; MMIM602; BMB603; MMIM608; MMIM609

courses.title: Biostatistics and Epidemiology 1
courses.description: This course introduces students to the basic concepts and principles of epidemiology and biostatistics. After a review of the history and development of epidemiology as basic science of public health, students will consider definitions of health, the determinants of health and the natural history of disease. They will then be introduced to th science of demography, measures of disease frequency and sources of data for measuring health outcomes. Students will distinguish descriptive epidemiology from ana epidemiology and they will then cover the key epidemiological study designs in a logical sequence from ecological and cross sectional studies to case-control and cohort studies, and randomized controlled trials. They will learn how to ask public health research questions, propose hypotheses and select appropriate study designs. They w apply their new learning to practical public health problems. They will be introduced to infectious disease epidemiology and outbreak investigation. The biostatistics sessi will deal with the interpretation of results obtained from the practical applications of statistics used in medical research including descriptive statistics and inferential statis

courses.title: Biostatistics and Epidemiology 2
courses.description: This course builds on the concepts and principles of epidemiology and biostatistics that students were introduced to in the first level. After a revision session covering he outcome measures, students will cover rate adjustment, cause, bias and confounding. They will then be introduced to screening and clinical trials. Students will have an opportunity to practice literature searches and critical appraisal. They will learn more about ethics in medical research and will have a revision session on scientific writin They will have sessions on chronic disease and injury epidemiology and will conclude with environmental epidemiology and an infectious disease case study. The biosta session deal with the interpretation of results obtained from the practical applications of statistics used in medical research including cohort studies and clinical trials.
